```{r gtg-setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
                      warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.2,
                      fig.align = "center", dpi = 72, fig.retina = 1, dev = "png", out.width = "100%")
```

This guide sets up a FLOSS operating model (OM) with growth morphs, samples it
by season, and tunes it to a target exploitation history. It is written for
simulation tests of length-based methods (LBSPR, LBB, fishblicc, FLicc), where
the way the OM generates length data decides whether a test is fair. The
equations are in the appendix at the end; each step in the main text refers to
them.

```
1 Why morphs  ->  2 Fishery and species  ->  3 Morph settings  ->  4 Build the OM
  ->  5 Check the morphs  ->  6 Tune  ->  7 Seasonal length samples  ->  8 Age samples
  ->  9 Export and fit  ->  Appendix: equations
```

```{r gtg-packages}
library(FLOSS)
library(ggplot2)
```

# 1 Why growth morphs

Gears select fish by length, not by age. Within an age, fast growers reach the
selected lengths first and are removed first, so the survivors of an exploited
cohort are smaller at age than the unfished cohort. This is the Rosa Lee
effect. A standard age-structured OM applies selectivity at age (the
selectivity at length averaged over the lengths of an age), which removes all
fish of an age at the same rate. The survivors then keep the unexploited
length distribution, and the length data are too long at a given level of
fishing. A length-based method fitted to such data sees too little mortality.
In earlier FLOSS runs, SPR from FLicc was biased by +20% to +100% for
fast-growing species and dome-shaped gears.

With `gtg`, `build_om()` follows growth-type groups (morphs) that differ in
asymptotic length (Linf) through each cohort's fishing history. The
age-structured OM is then run with the effective fishing mortality, weight and
maturity at age that result. The `FLStock` stays a standard FLR object, so
FLBRP, FLRef and mse work as before. The length samples are drawn from the
morphs in each fleet's catch.

The design follows the growth-type-group (GTG) LBSPR of Hordyk et al. (2016).
The same idea underlies the platoons of Stock Synthesis and the unit-structured
FLR implementation of M. Taylor (pers. comm.).

# 2 Fishery and species

The fishery has three gears: traps (dome-shaped, small fish), gillnet (dome,
medium fish) and linefish (logistic, large fish). We use the rabbitfish
*Siganus sutor*. It is short-lived and fast-growing, which is where the
morphs matter most.

```{r gtg-fishery}
fy <- load_fishery("reef_3fleets")
sp <- load_species("siganus_sutor")
unlist(sp$lh[c("linf", "k", "t0", "M", "tm", "tmax", "sigR", "rho", "s")])
unlist(sp$relq)
```

Catchability relative to Fmsy (`relq`) sets each gear's apical F as
$F_{f,y} = \text{relq}_f \, F_{MSY} \, E_{f,y}$ (methods appendix, section 2).
It is the main tuning parameter (section 6).

```{r gtg-sel, fig.height = 3.4}
FLRef::plot_sel_la(species_sel(sp), age_by = 1, len_by = 5)
```

# 3 Morph settings

`gtg_settings()` sets the number of morphs `n`, the range of the morph grid
in standard deviations (`maxsd`), and the total coefficient of variation (CV)
of Linf among fish, `cv`. The total CV is split into a between-morph part and
a within-morph part (Appendix A1). By default the within-morph CV is
`cv / sqrt(n)`, so more morphs give narrower morphs. The total spread is
always the `cv` you set.

```{r gtg-settings}
gs <- gtg_settings(n = 15, maxsd = 2.5, cv = 0.1)
unlist(gs)
```

`plot_gtg_linf()` shows the morph components, their mixture (dashed) and the
target normal distribution of Linf (solid). It works on a morph structure
before any OM is built:

```{r gtg-linf, fig.height = 3.6}
G <- FLOSS:::gtg_setup(sp, fy$fleets, gs)
plot_gtg_linf(G) + ggtitle(sp$species)
```

**Choosing `n` and `cv`.** A CV of 0.1 is the usual default in GTG-LBSPR and
FLicc. Values of 0.05–0.15 cover most teleosts. SPR converges as `n` grows:
from 15 to 25 morphs it changes by less than 1%, while 5 morphs give SPR a few
percent too low. Run time grows linearly with `n`, so 15 is a good default.
A quick check at the current F of each gear:

```{r gtg-n}
f_now <- c(traps = 0.6, gillnet = 0.2, linefish = 0.04)
vapply(c(5, 9, 15, 25), function(n)
  FLOSS:::gtg_spr(FLOSS:::gtg_setup(sp, fy$fleets, gtg_settings(n = n)), f_now), 0)
```

# 4 Build the operating model

`build_om()` takes `gtg` like any other setting. Recruitment variability
(`sigR`) and autocorrelation come from the species spec. Autocorrelation is
used only with `ar1 = TRUE`.

```{r gtg-build}
sp$lh$sigR <- 0.5
om <- build_om(sp, fy, nsim = 20, gtg = gs)
om
```

The morph part of the OM is in `om$gtg`:

- `G`: the morph structure (grid, lengths, weights, maturity and selectivity
  by morph and age);
- `spr`: the true equilibrium SPR by year and iteration, from the morphs;
- `fapic_full`: apical F by fleet, including the burn-in years;
- `refpts`: reference points of the morph equilibrium (Appendix A10);
- `refpts_flbrp`: the same from FLBRP on the fished exploitation pattern;
- `cwt`: catch weight at age by fleet.

```{r gtg-refpts}
round(om$gtg$refpts, 3)
round(om$gtg$refpts_flbrp, 3)
```

The two sets of reference points differ. In the morph equilibrium, weight,
maturity and effective selectivity at age change with F. FLBRP holds the
fished pattern fixed. `om$stock@refpts` uses the morph values.

# 5 Check the morphs

**Growth curves.** Line width shows each morph's share of the recruits; the
dashed line is the VB curve of the mean morph.

```{r gtg-growth, fig.height = 3.6}
plot_gtg_growth(om)
```

**Effective selectivity at age.** This is fleet F at age divided by its
maximum, in the first and last years, against the selectivity at age that an
age-based OM would use. All gears select young fast growers earlier than the
age-based curve suggests. At older ages, the fish left in the selected range
are fished down as F builds up, so effective selectivity at those ages falls
between the first and the last year.

```{r gtg-selplot}
plot_gtg_selectivity(om)
```

**Length at age (Rosa Lee).** Mean length at age in the population and in each
fleet's catch, in the last year. The direction depends on the shape of the
selectivity. A logistic gear removes the fast growers of an age first, so the
population mean falls below the VB curve (the classic Rosa Lee effect).
Dome-shaped gears, the traps and gillnet here, remove the slow growers that
stay in the selected range longer, while the fast growers outgrow it, so the
population mean at older ages rises above the VB curve. The catch of each gear
sits where its selectivity puts it: traps and gillnet catch the slow growers
of older ages, linefish the fast growers.

```{r gtg-lenage}
plot_gtg_lenage(om)
```

# 6 Tune the operating model

Tuning sets four things: the exploitation history (how far SPR falls), the
catch shares by gear, the recruitment variability, and the morph settings.
The OM is cheap to build with `nsim = 1` and `sigR = 0.01`, so it can be
tuned by searching over these settings.

**Exploitation history.** `plot_gtg_spr()` shows the true SPR by year, with SPR
at MSY of the morph equilibrium (dashed) and the 0.4 proxy (dotted).

```{r gtg-spr, fig.height = 3.6}
plot_gtg_spr(om)
```

To reach a target SPR at the end of the series, scale all `relq` values by a
common multiplier. The shares between gears stay fixed. The search below runs
on a deterministic OM (one iteration, no recruitment variation):

```{r gtg-tune}
final_spr <- function(mult, sp, years = 5) {
  s <- sp; s$relq <- lapply(sp$relq, `*`, mult); s$lh$sigR <- 0.01
  o <- build_om(s, fy, nsim = 1, gtg = gs)
  mean(utils::tail(c(o$gtg$spr), years))
}
target <- 0.3
mult <- uniroot(function(m) final_spr(m, sp) - target, c(0.2, 3), tol = 0.01)$root
round(mult, 3)
sp_tuned <- sp; sp_tuned$relq <- lapply(sp$relq, `*`, mult)
unlist(sp_tuned$relq)
```

**Catch shares.** Catch by gear follows from each gear's relq, its effort
history and what its selectivity overlaps with the stock. Change a single
gear's relq to shift the shares (in the FLicc paper, gillnet relq was raised
for emperor to give a stronger distortion from that gear).

```{r gtg-shares, fig.height = 3.2}
om_t <- build_om(sp_tuned, fy, nsim = 20, gtg = gs)
cs <- catch_fleet(om_t)
share <- sapply(cs, function(x) c(iterMedians(x[, ac(2016:2025)]))) /
  rowSums(sapply(cs, function(x) c(iterMedians(x[, ac(2016:2025)]))))
round(colMeans(share), 2)
plot_fleets(om_t, "catch")
```

**Recruitment.** `sp$lh$sigR` sets the variability of the lognormal
recruitment deviations. `sp$lh$rho` with `ar1 = TRUE` adds autocorrelation.
For short-lived species, a high sigmaR makes the length composition of any
single year far from equilibrium, which equilibrium-based methods cannot
follow. Common test values are 0.4 (Pons et al. 2019), 0.6 (Hordyk et al.
2014b; Rudd and Thorson 2018) and 0.74 with rho 0.43 (the meta-analytic
value; Thorson et al. 2014).

# 7 Seasonal length samples

A fishery operates all year. With morphs, fish grow and fast growers are
removed during the year, so a single mid-year sample distorts the length
composition. In the FLicc tests, SPR was biased by +27% to +61% with one
sample per year, +2% to +10% with four seasons, and about 0 with monthly
samples. `oem_settings(seasons = 12)` samples each month. Each month's catch
at age is the Baranov fraction of the annual catch (Appendix A6). Lengths are
read at the middle of the month from the morphs in the catch (Appendix A7).

```{r gtg-oem}
oem <- oem_settings(fy, seasons = 12, survey = NULL,
                    years = list(traps = c(2016, 2025), gillnet = c(2011, 2025),
                                 linefish = c(2006, 2025)),
                    lfd_ess_age = 30, lfd_ess_len = 300,
                    bio_n = c(traps = 150, gillnet = 0, linefish = 0),
                    bio_age_scheme = "random", bio_p_aged = 1, age_cv = 0)
dat <- sample_data(list(rabbitfish = om_t), oem, iters = 1:5, seed = 1)
head(dat$lfd)
```

`ess_age` is the number of clusters (stage 1, ages) and `ess_len` the number
of fish measured (stage 2) per gear and year. Both are split over the seasons
by the season shares of `season_design()` (equal by default). `season_design()`
can also set unequal shares, shifts in sampling over time and missing seasons.

```{r gtg-seasons, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_seasons(dat, iter = 1)
```

**Truth against samples.** `gtg_lfq()` gives the true catch-at-length by
fleet, year and season: the composition the samples are drawn from, without
sampling error (Appendix A9). `plot_gtg_lfq()` shows it with the samples (here
with the seasons weighted equally, as the samples are; see below):

```{r gtg-lfq, fig.height = 4.6}
plot_gtg_lfq(om_t, dat, iter = 1, years = c(2016, 2025), oem = oem, season_weights = "equal")
lq <- gtg_lfq(om_t, oem, iters = 1, years = 2025)
dim(lq$traps)                  # length x year x unit x season x area x iter
```

By default `gtg_lfq()` weights the seasons by their catch. Samples split
equally over the seasons give each month the same weight instead. For a
fast-growing species with high mortality, the catch falls through the year
while the fish grow, so the equally weighted samples are longer than the
catch-weighted truth. `season_weights = "equal"` gives the truth that matches
this design. With large samples, the mean lengths agree:

```{r gtg-weights}
o_big <- oem_settings(fy, seasons = 12, survey = NULL, lfd_ess_age = 5000, lfd_ess_len = 50000)
mean_len <- function(q) { L <- an(dimnames(q)$len) + 0.5; n <- c(seasonSums(q)); sum(L * n) / sum(n) }
set.seed(2)
l <- sample_lfd(om_t, o_big, iters = 1)
l <- l[l$year == 2025, ]
round(rbind(
  `truth, catch-weighted` = sapply(gtg_lfq(om_t, o_big, iters = 1, years = 2025), mean_len),
  `truth, equal seasons` = sapply(gtg_lfq(om_t, o_big, iters = 1, years = 2025,
                                          season_weights = "equal"), mean_len),
  samples = (tapply((l$len_mm / 10 + 0.5) * l$n, l$source, sum) / tapply(l$n, l$source, sum))[fy$fleets]), 2)
```

To weight samples by catch, set the season shares of `season_design()` in
proportion to the seasonal catch, or raise the samples to the catch
(`lfd_aggregate()`).

**Why monthly sampling matters.** Fish grow through the year. A single
mid-year sample reads every fish at the same point in its growth, so the
cohorts appear as sharp modes. Real catches, taken all year, smear the modes
over a year's growth. Monthly samples reproduce that smearing. A
length-based method that assumes continuous fishing (FLicc, LBSPR) expects the
smeared composition:

```{r gtg-timing, fig.height = 3.4}
lfd_S <- function(S) {
  o <- oem_settings(fy, seasons = S, survey = NULL, lfd_ess_age = 5000, lfd_ess_len = 50000)
  set.seed(3)
  l <- sample_lfd(om_t, o, iters = 1)
  l <- stats::aggregate(n ~ len_mm, l[l$year == 2025 & l$source == "traps", ], sum)
  data.frame(L = l$len_mm / 10 + 0.5, p = l$n / sum(l$n),
             what = paste(S, if (S == 1) "season (mid-year)" else "seasons"))
}
q <- gtg_lfq(om_t, o_big, fleets = "traps", iters = 1, years = 2025, season_weights = "equal")$traps
tr <- data.frame(L = an(dimnames(q)$len) + 0.5, p = c(seasonSums(q)) / sum(q), what = "truth (equal seasons)")
ggplot(rbind(lfd_S(1), lfd_S(12)), aes(L, p, colour = what)) +
  geom_step(direction = "mid") +
  geom_line(data = tr, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#D95F02", "#1B9E77")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(10, 40)) +
  labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Proportion", colour = NULL, title = "Traps, 2025",
       subtitle = "black: truth; large samples (50,000 fish) with one or twelve seasons") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# 8 Age samples (age-length keys)

`sample_bio()` draws fish from each gear's catch by season. Their lengths
come from the morphs, as for the length samples. Ageing can be random
(`bio_age_scheme = "random"`, a share `bio_p_aged` of the fish) or stratified
by length (`"stratified"`, up to `bio_n_per_bin` fish per length class).
Conditional age at length is not changed by length-based selection of the
aged fish, so either scheme gives an unbiased conditional key. A von
Bertalanffy curve fitted directly to age-length pairs from a selective gear
is biased; FLicc's internal ALK option accounts for selection.

```{r gtg-bio, fig.height = 3.6}
plot_bio(dat, iter = 1, what = "age_length")
```

# 9 Export and fit

`as_flr()` returns the samples as FLR objects: length compositions by gear
(`FLQuants`, length x year, summed over seasons), catch by gear and the life
history (`FLPar`, with maturity L50 and L95 as the OM uses them and weight in
kg). These go straight into FLicc:

```{r gtg-flr}
x <- as_flr(dat, iter = 1)
names(x)
x$lhpar
```

```{r gtg-flicc, eval = requireNamespace("FLicc", quietly = TRUE), fig.height = 3.6}
yrs <- ac(2016:2025)
lf <- FLQuants(lapply(x$lfd[fy$fleets], function(q) {
  z <- FLQuant(0, dimnames = list(len = dimnames(q)$len, year = yrs))
  yy <- intersect(dimnames(q)$year, yrs); z[, yy] <- q[, yy]; z }))
cbg <- FLQuants(lapply(x$catch[fy$fleets], function(q) q[, yrs]))
fit <- FLicc::fiticc(lf, FLicc::stocklen(lf, x$lhpar),
                     sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "normal", "logistic"), catch_by_gear = cbg,
                     settings = list(CVL = 0.1, pop_model = "gtg", obs_model = "dm"), verbose = FALSE)
est <- FLicc::spr_ci_flicc(fit)
est$year <- as.numeric(est$year)
tru <- as.data.frame(om_t$gtg$spr[, yrs, , , , 1])
ggplot(est, aes(year, spr)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(colour = "FLicc")) +
  geom_line(data = tru, aes(an(as.character(year)), data, colour = "OM (morphs)")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(FLicc = "#08519c", `OM (morphs)` = "black")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = an(yrs)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "SPR", colour = NULL, subtitle = "FLicc fit (95% interval) and true SPR, iteration 1") +
  theme_bw()
```

For SSB relative to SSBmsy, SPR converts with the OM's steepness and
Beverton–Holt relationship (Appendix A10).

# 10 What is not covered

- **Projections (MSE).** The OM's FLStock is standard, but the morph
  composition is fixed by the historical F. Projecting with morphs needs the
  tracker stepped each year with the projected fleet F; this is not yet
  implemented. Projections with the FLStock as it stands use the last years'
  effective selectivity, weight and maturity at age.
- **Selectivity treatments** (changes of gear selectivity over time) are not
  yet combined with morphs.
- **Survey samples** use the age-based keys of `FLRef`, without morphs.
- **Sex structure** uses the FLStock unit dimension. Morphs are tracked outside
  the FLStock, so they could be combined with sex structure, but this is not
  implemented.

# Appendix: methods and equations

## A1 Morph grid and the CV of Linf

**Idea.** Fish differ in asymptotic length. Recruits are split into $G$
morphs on a grid of standard normal values. Each morph has its own Linf, and
lengths still vary a little within a morph. The total spread among fish is
the CV set by the user.

Grid and recruitment shares, for morph $g = 1, \dots, G$:

$$
z_g = -z_{max} + \frac{2 z_{max}\,(g-1)}{G-1}, \qquad
p_g = \frac{\phi(z_g)}{\sum_h \phi(z_h)},
$$

with $\phi$ the standard normal density and $z_{max}$ = `maxsd`. The grid is
rescaled so that its weighted SD is exactly 1 (truncation at $\pm z_{max}$
would otherwise narrow it):
$\tilde z_g = z_g / \sqrt{\sum_h p_h z_h^2}$.

Split of the total CV into a between-morph and a within-morph part (after
M. Taylor's FLR platoon code):

$$
CV_w = \frac{CV}{\sqrt{G}}, \qquad CV_b = \sqrt{CV^2 - CV_w^2}, \qquad
L_{\infty,g} = L_\infty\,(1 + CV_b\,\tilde z_g).
$$

The mixture of within-morph normals then has variance
$\approx (CV\,L_\infty)^2$ (`plot_gtg_linf()`).

## A2 Growth, weight and maturity by morph

All morphs share $k$, $t_0$ and $M$:

$$
L_g(t) = L_{\infty,g}\left(1 - e^{-k(t - t_0)}\right),
\qquad w_{g,a} = c\,\alpha\,L_g(a)^{\beta},
$$

with $c$ a scaling that makes the mean weight at age equal that of the
calibrated FLBRP. Weight at the start of the year uses $L_g(a)$; catch weight
uses the mid-year length $L_g(a + 0.5)$. Maturity is logistic in length, with
$L_{50} = L(t_m)$ and $L_{95} = L(t_m + 1)$ from the mean VB curve:

$$
m_{g,a} = \left[1 + \exp\!\left(-\ln 19\,\frac{L_g(a) - L_{50}}{L_{95} - L_{50}}\right)\right]^{-1},
\qquad m_{g,0} = 0 .
$$

## A3 Selectivity by morph

Each fleet's selectivity at length $s_f(L)$ is logistic, normal or
double-normal (the FLRef shapes), scaled to a maximum of 1. A morph's
selectivity at age is read at its mid-year length:

$$
s_{f,g,a} = s_f\!\left(L_g(a + 0.5)\right).
$$

## A4 Tracking morphs through the fishing history

**Idea.** Morphs are followed per recruit. Each cohort keeps its morph shares
at recruitment and loses fast growers faster wherever a gear selects them.
The morph composition depends only on the F history, not on the number of
recruits.

With apical fleet F $F_{f,y}$:

$$
Z_{g,a,y} = M + \sum_f s_{f,g,a}\,F_{f,y},
$$

$$
\ell_{g,0,y} = p_g, \qquad
\ell_{g,a+1,y+1} = \ell_{g,a,y}\,e^{-Z_{g,a,y}}, \qquad
\ell_{g,A,y+1} \mathrel{+}= \ell_{g,A,y}\,e^{-Z_{g,A,y}},
$$

with $A$ the plus group. The first year starts at the equilibrium at its F:
$\ell_{g,a} = p_g \exp(-\sum_{j<a} Z_{g,j})$, and the plus group divided by
$1 - e^{-Z_{g,A}}$.

## A5 From morphs to the age-structured OM

**Idea.** The FLStock needs one F, weight and maturity per age. Effective F is
chosen so that the age-structured OM has the same survival as the morphs.
Weight and maturity are the morph averages for the fish that are present.
Recruitment then scales everything.

Numbers and survivors per recruit, effective F:

$$
N_{a,y} = \sum_g \ell_{g,a,y}, \qquad
F^{e}_{a,y} = -\ln\!\left(\frac{\sum_g \ell_{g,a,y}\,e^{-Z_{g,a,y}}}{N_{a,y}}\right) - M .
$$

Weight and maturity at age (maturity as a weight-weighted mean, so SSB
matches):

$$
W_{a,y} = \frac{\sum_g \ell_{g,a,y}\,w_{g,a}}{N_{a,y}}, \qquad
\text{mat}_{a,y} = \frac{\sum_g \ell_{g,a,y}\,w_{g,a}\,m_{g,a}}{\sum_g \ell_{g,a,y}\,w_{g,a}} .
$$

Catch by fleet, catch shares and fleet F at age:

$$
C_{f,g,a,y} = \ell_{g,a,y}\,\frac{s_{f,g,a}F_{f,y}}{Z_{g,a,y}}\left(1 - e^{-Z_{g,a,y}}\right),
\qquad
\pi_{f,a,y} = \frac{\sum_g C_{f,g,a,y}}{\sum_{f'}\sum_g C_{f',g,a,y}},
\qquad F_{f,a,y} = \pi_{f,a,y}\,F^{e}_{a,y}.
$$

Catch weight by fleet is $\sum_g C_{f,g,a,y}\,w_{g}(a+0.5) / \sum_g C_{f,g,a,y}$.
FLasher projects the FLStock with $F^e$ and the stock-recruitment
relationship, so numbers, catch and SSB at age agree with the morph dynamics.
The only approximation is in the plus group, where cohorts mix.

## A6 Seasonal catch

**Idea.** Within a year, catch at age is spread over equal seasons in
proportion to the numbers caught in each season under constant $Z$.

For $S$ seasons with limits $t_{s-1} = (s-1)/S$ and $t_s = s/S$:

$$
\varphi_{a,s} = \frac{e^{-Z_{a,y}\,t_{s-1}} - e^{-Z_{a,y}\,t_s}}{1 - e^{-Z_{a,y}}},
\qquad C_{f,a,y,s} = \varphi_{a,s}\,C_{f,a,y},
$$

with $Z_{a,y} = F^e_{a,y} + M$ from the FLStock and $\sum_s \varphi_{a,s} = 1$.

## A7 Age-length key of a fleet's catch

**Idea.** Lengths in the catch at age come from the morphs in that catch. They
are read at the time of the sample, with a small normal spread within each
morph, and the gear selects on that length.

For length bin $[l, l + \Delta)$ at time $t$ in the year (the middle of the
season):

$$
P_{g,a,l}(t) = \Phi\!\left(\frac{l + \Delta - L_g(a+t)}{CV_w\,L_g(a+t)}\right)
             - \Phi\!\left(\frac{l - L_g(a+t)}{CV_w\,L_g(a+t)}\right),
$$

$$
K_{f,a,l,y}(t) = \frac{s_f(l + \Delta/2)\,\sum_g C_{f,g,a,y}\,P_{g,a,l}(t)}
                      {\sum_{l'} s_f(l' + \Delta/2)\,\sum_g C_{f,g,a,y}\,P_{g,a,l'}(t)} .
$$

The morph weights $C_{f,g,a,y}$ are the morphs in the fleet's annual catch at
age. Depletion of fast growers within the year enters through the season's
length at age, not through a change in morph shares within the year.

## A8 Two-stage length sampling

**Idea.** Fish are caught and measured in clusters (trips, sets), and fish in
the same cluster are alike in size. Stage 1 draws the ages of the clusters,
stage 2 the lengths of the measured fish.

The effective sample sizes are split over the seasons by the season shares
$q_s$: $n^{a}_s = q_s\,n^{a}$ and $n^{L}_s = q_s\,n^{L}$. Then

$$
\mathbf{x}^{a}_s \sim \text{Mult}\!\left(n^a_s,\; C_{f,\cdot,y,s}\right),
\qquad
\mathbf{x}^{L}_s \sim \text{Mult}\!\left(n^L_s,\; \sum_a \frac{x^a_{a,s}}{n^a_s}\,K_{f,a,\cdot,y}(t_s)\right),
$$

with $t_s$ the middle of season $s$. Fewer clusters give overdispersed length
compositions at the same number of fish measured (methods appendix, section 6).

## A9 True catch-at-length

Without sampling error, catch at length by fleet, year and season is

$$
C^{L}_{f,l,y,s} = \sum_a \varphi_{a,s}\,C_{f,a,y}\,K_{f,a,l,y}(t_s)
$$

(`gtg_lfq()`). Summed over lengths it equals the fleet's catch at age within
the length range.

## A10 SPR and reference points of the morph equilibrium

At constant fleet F $\mathbf{F} = (F_f)$, the equilibrium per-recruit numbers
$\ell_{g,a}(\mathbf{F})$ follow from A4. Spawning biomass per recruit, SPR
and yield per recruit:

$$
\psi(\mathbf{F}) = \sum_{g,a} \ell_{g,a}\,w_{g,a}\,m_{g,a}, \qquad
\text{SPR}(\mathbf{F}) = \frac{\psi(\mathbf{F})}{\psi(\mathbf{0})},
$$

$$
\text{YPR}(\mathbf{F}) = \sum_f \sum_{g,a} \ell_{g,a}\,\frac{s_{f,g,a}F_f}{Z_{g,a}}
\left(1 - e^{-Z_{g,a}}\right) w_g(a + 0.5).
$$

The true SPR in year $y$ (`om$gtg$spr`) is $\text{SPR}(\mathbf{F}_y)$ at that
year's fleet F. With the OM's Beverton–Holt relationship $R = aS/(b + S)$,
equilibrium SSB and yield along the fleet F pattern $\mathbf{F} = x\,\mathbf{p}$
(the median pattern of the last three years) are

$$
S(x) = a\,\psi(x\mathbf{p}) - b, \qquad Y(x) = \frac{S(x)}{\psi(x\mathbf{p})}\,\text{YPR}(x\mathbf{p}),
$$

$x_{MSY} = \arg\max_x Y(x)$, $B_{MSY} = S(x_{MSY})$, $B_0 = a\,\psi(\mathbf{0}) - b$
and $\text{SPR}_{MSY} = \text{SPR}(x_{MSY}\mathbf{p})$. $F_{MSY}$ is reported on
the FLStock's fbar scale, as the mean of $F^e_a$ over the fbar ages. Relative
SSB follows from SPR with steepness $h = 0.2(b + B_0)/(b + 0.2B_0)$:

$$
\frac{S}{B_0} = \frac{4h\,\text{SPR} - (1 - h)}{5h - 1} .
$$

## Notation

| Symbol | Meaning | FLOSS |
|---|---|---|
| $G$, $z_{max}$ | number of morphs, grid range in SD | `gtg_settings(n, maxsd)` |
| $CV$, $CV_b$, $CV_w$ | total, between- and within-morph CV of Linf | `cv`, `cv_between`, `cv_res` |
| $p_g$ | share of recruits in morph $g$ | `om$gtg$G$recP` |
| $L_{\infty,g}$ | asymptotic length of morph $g$ | `om$gtg$G$linf_g` |
| $s_f(L)$ | selectivity at length of fleet $f$ | `sp$sel` |
| $F_{f,y}$ | apical F of fleet $f$ | `om$fapic`, `om$gtg$fapic_full` |
| $\ell_{g,a,y}$ | numbers per recruit by morph and age | `gtg_track()` |
| $F^{e}_{a,y}$ | effective F at age | `harvest(om$stock)` |
| $\varphi_{a,s}$ | share of the annual catch at age in season $s$ | `season_catch_frac()` |
| $K_{f,a,l,y}(t)$ | age-length key of fleet $f$'s catch | `gtg_keys()` |
| $C^L_{f,l,y,s}$ | true catch at length | `gtg_lfq()` |
